title: Static clicking sensitivity starting range
summary: For static clicking, a practical starting range is about 35-55 cm/360, usually leaning slower when tiny-target landing stability is the main goal.
why: Static clicking rewards precise landings and small cleanup demand, so players often benefit from a somewhat steadier range than fast reactive work.
A slower setup can make tiny-target placement and finish quality easier to control as long as the scenario does not become physically cumbersome.
actions: Start around 43 cm/360 and slow down slightly if tiny targets expose overflicks and shaky landings.
If every target change feels physically heavy even when your path is good, test a modestly faster step.
Evaluate time-to-kill and first-landing quality together, not flick speed in isolation.
avoid: Do not chase stability so far that wide target spreads become physically awkward.
Avoid treating one exact static sens as sacred across every clicking task.

drills.label: Static landing quality check
drills.reason: Static tasks make overflicks and shaky cleanup very visible when the sensitivity is slightly off.

evidence.claim: Lower sensitivities can offer more precision for small movements, but should still be chosen as a tool for the task rather than preserved blindly.
evidence.excerpt: Using a lower sensitivity makes it easier to make smaller movements more accurately.
